title: Recall the Factor Theorem Condition
text:
The Factor Theorem states: $(x - a)$ is a factor of $f(x)$ if and only if $f(a) = 0$.

We found that $f(2) = 0$.

title: Apply the Theorem
text:
Since $f(2) = 0$, the condition of the Factor Theorem is satisfied.

This means $(x - 2)$ divides $f(x)$ exactly with no remainder.

title: The Answer
text:
Yes, $(x - 2)$ is a factor of $x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6$.

In fact, we can write: $x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6 = (x - 2)(x^2 - 2x - 3) = (x - 2)(x - 3)(x + 1)$
